title: Uniform spectral-cluster pseudodistance equivalence on compact boundaryless Riemannian manifolds of dimension at least two
source_title: A necessary and sufficient condition for probabilistic continuity on a boundaryless compact Riemannian manifold
author: Rafik Imekraz
difficulty_reason: An on-diagonal Weyl estimate alone loses the quadratic separation factor for points arbitrarily closer than one wavelength. Section6 retains mixed spectral-projector derivatives through the two-point cancellation and combines that small-scale argument with intermediate and separated-point estimates by widening the fixed cluster. The complete Appendix supplies the required differentiated spectral asymptotic from the named analytic foundations, so the source-specific scale control remains an obligation rather than a direct use of a continuity theorem.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Independent Theorem10: compact boundaryless Riemannian manifold of dimension d>=2, square-root Laplacian spectral clusters(Kn-K,Kn], all n>=1 and all K>=K0. Their dimension-normalized squared eigenfunction-difference pseudodistance is uniformly equivalent to min(1,Kn times geodesic distance), with constants depending only on the manifold. Complete new far/intermediate/near diagonal proofs, finite-atlas geodesic double integration and Bessel positivity argument23–30 read; all required AppendixB derivative-Weyl proof55–58 retained and read. Existing Hörmander off-diagonal estimates, Canzani–Hanin local derivative asymptotics, Bin Bernstein bound, Tauberian lemma and Whitehead convexity radius are explicit research foundations. Proposition12 writes the shifted cluster(Kn,Kn+K] in one equality despite the defined(Kn-K,Kn]; applying the same supplied endpoint bounds to the defined cluster is bounded interval bookkeeping and leaves the K-dominance argument identical. Suppressed absolute-value bars in derivative remainder displays have their preceding uniform O meaning. This single substantial spectral-geometric claim is not the probabilistic continuity theorem, sphere parameter variant or Riemannian metric universality corollary; no dimension-one or boundary extrapolation.
